pulls.title: [32.x] Finalise 32.1
validation: don't accept txs to the mempool while loading a snapshot
pulls.body:
`ActivateSnapshot` checks that the mempool is empty before it starts, but `PopulateAndValidateSnapshot` then runs without `cs_main`, which takes minutes on mainnet. A transaction entering the mempool in that window (e.g. through `sendrawtransaction`) hits the assert in `AddChainstate`:

```
Assertion failed: (!prev_chainstate.m_mempool || prev_chainstate.m_mempool->size() == 0), function AddChainstate, file validation.cpp, line 6201.
```

By then the base blockhash file has been written, so the node needs `-reindex` to start again.

This sets a flag on `ChainstateManager` while `ActivateSnapshot` runs, and `AcceptToMemoryPool` and `ProcessNewPackage` reject with `snapshot-loading` while it's set. `testmempoolaccept` still works. A second `loadtxoutset` started while one is running is also rejected.

`test_mempool_blocked_during_load` in `feature_assumeutxo.py` pauses the load through a FIFO, checks that `sendrawtransaction` and `submitpackage` are rejected and the mempool stays empty, then lets the load finish. On master the transaction is accepted and the node aborts. The test is skipped where `os.mkfifo` isn't available.

pulls.title: wallet: only rebroadcast transactions originating from the wallet
pulls.body:
As explained in #3828, rebroadcast of transactions paying the wallet (but not spending any wallet inputs) is a privacy leak, since anyone can generate these, choose a low fee, and observe who rebroadcasts them. 
While it is somewhat intuitive that submitting transactions has privacy implications - at least until confirmation - this is manageable by various strategies (switching to privacy networks for a while, using private broadcast, making sure it confirms before rebroadcast). However, I find it rather unexpected that just passively running a node with a wallet loaded can lead to a loss of privacy as well.

This PR stops rebroadcasting transactions that don't spend any wallet inputs. For the same reason, they are also no longer re-added to the mempool on startup or after an import: otherwise our node might be the only one still having a transaction the rest of the network has dropped, which can be detected with active probing (e.g. by submitting a child).

This does have the trade-off that receivers (who have an incentive to get paid) will now need to manually resubmit transactions if the transaction doesn't confirm and the sender doesn't rebroadcast, but I think it is worth the privacy benefit.

An alternative approach is https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36380, although these could also be combined (make rebroadcast optional, but never rebroadcast non-originating transactions)

Fixes #3828

pulls.title: mining: move getblocktemplate cache into BlockTemplateManager
pulls.body:
Follow-up to #35675. This addresses the `getblocktemplate` part of the "Remove remaining global states" TODO in #33758, as suggested in https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/35675#pullrequestreview-5299625960.

`getblocktemplate` reuses its last template until the tip changes, or until the mempool changes and the template is more than 5 seconds old. That cache currently lives in four function-local statics, which:

- live as long as the process, so the cached `CBlockIndex*` can outlive its `ChainstateManager` (as in unit tests);
- rely on `cs_main` being held, which nothing checks;
- can't be unit tested.

This PR moves the cache into `BlockTemplateManager`, in three commits:

1. **rpc:** refactors the statics in place into a `CachedBlockTemplate` struct and a `GetNewOrCachedBlockTemplate()` helper, `GUARDED_BY(::cs_main)`. The template's `hashPrevBlock` replaces the cached `CBlockIndex*`, and the 5 seconds becomes `GBT_TEMPLATE_REBUILD_INTERVAL`.
2. **refactor:** moves them into `BlockTemplateManager`. It's easiest to review with `git show --color-moved=dimmed-zebra --color-moved-ws=allow-indentation-change`.
3. **test:** adds a unit test for each rebuild rule and for the retry after a failed build.

No behavior change is intended, and only `getblocktemplate` uses the cache. It uses `cs_main` rather than its own mutex, since the RPC already holds it and building a template takes it anyway.

pulls.title: contrib: exclude inactive keys from the binary quorum by default
pulls.body:
**Problem:** The binary verifier counts signatures from expired and revoked keys toward `--min-good-sigs`.
Enough of these signatures can satisfy the threshold without any active signing key, and they are returned as good signatures.

**Fix:** Warn about expired and revoked signatures and exclude them from threshold counting by default.
For historical verification, expired signatures can count toward the threshold with `--allow-expired` or `BINVERIFY_ALLOW_EXPIRED`, including signatures created after key expiry. Revoked signatures remain excluded.
Expired signatures are reported separately, including in the `expired_sigs` field in successful JSON output.

The decision uses GnuPG’s current key status from the local keyring, even if the signature was created while the key was active.

This was found and disclosed responsibly by the Red Team 🟥.

pulls.title: validation: don't treat snapshot block as linked on startup
pulls.body:
Background sync requests blocks up to and including the snapshot block from several peers at once, so the snapshot block can be stored before one of its ancestors. `ReceivedBlockTransactions()` then keeps it in `m_blocks_unlinked`, but that isn't persisted. On restart `LoadBlockIndex()` gives it the hardcoded `m_chain_tx_count`, `PopulateBlockIndexCandidates()` makes it a background candidate, and `FindMostWorkChain()` walks back to its parent, which has no chain tx count:

```
Assertion failed: (pindexTest->HaveNumChainTxs() || pindexTest->nHeight == 0), function FindMostWorkChain, file validation.cpp, line 3217.
```

It needs a restart in that window, so it should be rare, but after that the node aborts on every start. The only ways out I found are `-reindex-chainstate` or `-reindex`, and both delete the snapshot chainstate.

Fix this by adding the snapshot block to `m_blocks_unlinked` on startup if an ancestor is missing, and not making it a background candidate until then. Both are needed, without the first one background validation stalls. A node that is already stuck starts with the fix and finishes background validation without a reindex.

The new step in `feature_assumeutxo.py` restarts the node after the snapshot block is submitted out of order, and fails on master. I also reproduced it over p2p with a test peer that withholds the snapshot block's parent.

These are the two changes from #35307 (closed, the motivation there was `submitblock` before `loadtxoutset`) without its blockfile and VerifyDB changes. cyb3ralbert hit the same assertion while testing #36452 (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36452#issuecomment-6464524112), which is still needed when the snapshot tip is at the snapshot block. #36149 drops the `BLOCK_HAVE_DATA` check in the branch right below, so whichever is merged second should match it.

pulls.title: mempool: keep prioritisetransaction deltas within MAX_MONEY
pulls.body:
`prioritisetransaction` takes `fee_delta` as any int64. `CTxMemPool::PrioritiseTransaction` stacks deltas with `SaturatingAdd`, so the accumulated delta and the modified fee can go up to `INT64_MAX`. The cluster mempool then adds modified fees of several transactions together in `FeeFrac` (util/feefrac.h:108) without overflow checks.

For example, with a parent and child in the mempool:

```
prioritisetransaction <parent> 0 4611686018427387904
prioritisetransaction <child> 0 9223372036854775807
```

- `getmempoolcluster` reports `chunkfee: -46116860184.27356705`
- `getblocktemplate` contains neither transaction, and the next block mined has only the coinbase
- UBSan: `feefrac.h:108:13: runtime error: signed integer overflow`, reached from linearization via `getrawmempool`

There's no use for a delta larger than the total money supply, so this:

- rejects `fee_delta` outside `-MAX_MONEY..MAX_MONEY` in the RPC with "fee_delta out of range"
- clamps the accumulated delta to `-MAX_MONEY..MAX_MONEY` in `PrioritiseTransaction`, which also covers deltas loaded from mempool.dat, and updates the modified fee by the change in the clamped delta

With each modified fee bounded by 2 * MAX_MONEY, cluster sums stay far away from int64 limits.

The new `test_fee_delta_limits` in `mining_prioritisetransaction.py` checks the RPC range error, that stacked deltas stop at `MAX_MONEY`, that the chunk fees add up, and that both transactions are in the block template. It fails on master ("No exception raised"). `mempool_persist.py`, `mempool_packages.py`, `rpc_packages.py` and the miner/rbf/txpackage unit tests pass.

AI tools were used to help find this issue and to prepare the patch and test.

pulls.title: fuzz: push messages to one of m_nodes in connman target
pulls.body:
The connman fuzz target never exercised `m_nodes` peers with queued messages, as their message queue is always empty. The most they ever had to send was handshake bytes in the case of v2 peers, so the socket handler only ever waited for SendEvent, and sent data, during a v2 handshake.

Fix this by pushing messages to one of the `m_nodes` peers instead of `random_node`, which is never added to connman.

pulls.title: p2p: replace full outbound peers that don't support tx relay (take 2)
pulls.body:
Picks up #28538

Outbound-full-relay slots should be used by peers that actually relay transactions, besides #28538 see #16418 and #28371 for the motivation. So try to replace peers that are not relaying txs with peers that do.

The approach differs from the original PR in a few details in response to some of the review comments there:

- A replacement is connected before the peer is evicted. The original PR disconnected a non-tx-relaying peer once all full outbound slots were filled. Reviewers preferred having a replacement available first (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#issuecomment-1883481846). Now an extra outbound-full-relay connection is requested, like the extra network-specific peers, and the existing eviction of extra outbound peers prefers peers that don't relay txs.
- Peers not relaying txs don't get `m_protect`. Otherwise they could stay forever (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#discussion_r1443336121), and ignoring the protection was rejected in the same thread (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#discussion_r1443312604).
- An only peer on a network is not replaced. Otherwise the network-specific extra connections and this logic would keep replacing each other (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#issuecomment-1883481846). This also covers the `-maxconnections=1` case (https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/28538#discussion_r1417178196).

Nothing is changed in `-blocksonly` mode or during IBD. The rename commit and the functional test are taken from the original PR with some changes to match the new behavior.

pulls.body:
`_GLIBCXX_USE_DEPRECATED` is defined by default, disable it, which saves a few bytes worth of debug symbols.

> Defined to the value 1 by default. Not configurable. ABI-changing.
> Turning this off removes older ARM-style iostreams code, and other

> for different -std options.

See: https://gcc.gnu.org/onlinedocs/libstdc++/manual/using_macros.html.

pulls.title: torcontrol: escape backslashes in -torpassword
pulls.body:
With `HASHEDPASSWORD` authentication, `TorController::protocolinfo_cb` sends the password as a quoted string, `AUTHENTICATE "<password>"` (torcontrol.cpp:667). It escapes `"` but not `\`.

Tor parses that argument as a control-spec QuotedString, where a backslash escapes the next character. So:

- `-torpassword=pa\ss` reaches Tor as `pass`, authentication fails and no onion service is created
- `-torpassword=pass\` escapes the closing quote, so the command is malformed

This escapes backslashes before quotes.

The new `test_password_escaping` in `feature_torcontrol.py` uses the mock control server with `HASHEDPASSWORD` and `-torpassword=pa\ss"word\`, and checks the exact `AUTHENTICATE` line. On master it gets `AUTHENTICATE "pa\ss\"word\"`, with the fix `AUTHENTICATE "pa\\ss\"word\\"`.

Tested against Tor 0.4.9.12 with `HashedControlPassword` set for `pa\ss"word\`: on master bitcoind logs "tor: Authentication failed", with this change authentication succeeds and ADD_ONION creates the onion service.

AI tools were used to help find this issue and to prepare the patch and test.

pulls.title: ci: test cross-built macos arm64 binaries
pulls.body:
Currently we have some macos cross-built binaries, which are using depends as opposed to brew in the native macos builds, but these binaries are not being tested, culminating in silent breakages like #35771

Build `test_bitcoin-qt` in `macos_cross`, and test the binaries in a subsequent job.

the macos_cross job is removed from `ci-matrix` as otherwise the new `macos-cross-arm64` test job has to wait for all matrix jobs to finish (successfully) before running. This includes some of our slow jobs, and will needlessly inflate CI runtimes.

Doing this does add some more boilerplate into ci.yml, but IMO this is acceptable (and the best option currently).

pulls.title: rpc: reset id and version per batch element
pulls.body:
In a JSON-RPC batch, an element that is not an object gets an error reply with the id and version of the element before it.

`ExecuteHTTPRPC` uses one request object for the whole batch. `parse()` throws on a non-object before it resets `id` and `m_json_version`. For `[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"getblockcount","id":"X"}, 2]` the reply has two objects with `"id":"X"`, one with a result and one with an error. If the first element is a notification, the error is dropped. I reset both fields at the top of `parse()`, so the error is the one the first element of a batch already gets. The new case in `interface_rpc.py` fails on master and passes with this change.

pulls.title: wallet: extend -walletbroadcast to allow initial send only
pulls.body:
`-walletbroadcast` was a boolean `0` or `1` meaning either "do not broadcast transactions or "initial broadcast plus periodic re-broadcast (every 12-36 hours)".

Add a new possible value `initialonly` which would allow the user to configure the wallet to do the initial broadcast only and not to do the periodic rebroadcasts.

No new configuration options and no change in default behavior.
